title: Stop batcher oscillation by aligning timers and improving eviction handling
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Production customers on Hosted and Dedicated reported sustained suppression of short, latency-sensitive requests after prolonged mixed-length load. Investigation shows a feedback loop between host-level timer drift and aggressive KV-cache eviction resets that causes the continuous batcher to oscillate: the batcher repeatedly closes and re-opens admission windows, amplifying queueing for short flows and increasing long-context tail latency. This ticket implements fixes to stop the oscillation and restore short-request velocity while preserving batching efficiency for long-context workloads.

Observed behavior:
- Small request QPS drops by 60-80% during mixed-length waves lasting >5 minutes; long-context requests consume batch resources.
- 95th/99th latency for short flows increases 4-6x during episodes.
- Hosts show periodic spikes of KV eviction events coincident with batch admission window resets.
- Problem reproduced in Hosted and Dedicated clusters; Private customers with maintenance windows reported correlated regressions.

Root cause hypothesis validated:
1) Host-level timer drift between the scheduler tick and the continuous-batcher's admission loop causes misaligned closing windows under high load, producing premature batch seals for small requests.
2) Eviction logic currently resets prefetch/kv state synchronously and immediately signals admission lower-bound, which in the presence of misaligned ticks results in a feedback loop where eviction->admission-tighten->queue-growth->more-eviction occurs.
3) The admission algorithm lacks an explicit shortflow preservation path (a small-request priority token) so short flows starve during oscillation.

Proposed fixes (implementation plan):
A) Switch batcher tick source to a monotonic, host-anchored clock to eliminate cross-host timer drift effects (align admission/tick loop).
B) Introduce eviction debounce (200ms default) and make eviction resets idempotent for prefetch windows to avoid spurious admission tightening during transient spikes.
C) Add a shortflow-immortalize admission path: a lightweight per-tenant token bucket that guarantees capacity for small requests under bursty mixed-length workloads (configurable via feature flag).
D) Add an adaptive backoff that prevents immediate clamp-down of admission after an eviction reset; instead apply smoothing over a 1s window.
E) Telemetry and guarding: surface short-vs-long flow token consumption metrics, batch close rate, eviction rate, and host tick skew; add alert on sustained shortflow-QPS drop (>30% for 3 minutes).

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for eviction debounce and idempotence behavior.
- Integration tests in local cluster simulating mixed-length waves with configurable clock skew.
- Canary rollout in Hosted: enable fixes behind feature flag on 3% of hosts, use dark metrics to compare short QPS, batch sizes and 99p latencies.
- Dedicated customer staging trials: coordinate with two impacted customers for controlled canary.
- Private: provide patch and upgrade instructions; include opt-in flag for air-gapped installs.
- Chaos tests: introduce synthetic timer drift and KV eviction storms in staging to ensure fixes stop oscillation.

Rollout and mitigation strategy:
- Feature-flagged merge to main; deploy to canary pool with 3% traffic. Monitor defined KPIs for 48 hours.
- If regressions occur, toggle feature flag off (instant rollback).
- If canary stable, increase to 25% then full rollout over 72 hours.
- Publish runbook section for oncall: steps to toggle shortflow-immortalize, check eviction debouncing status, and gather diagnostic metrics (links below).

Deliverables:
- Code: batcher tick refactor + eviction debounce + admission token bucket (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423).
- Tests: unit and integration suites added under runtime/batcher/tests.
- Telemetry: dashboards and alerts (Grafana: dashboards/shortflow-protection) and new metrics (shortflow_token_usage, batch_close_rate, eviction_debounce_hits, host_tick_skew).
- Runbook: internal runbook entry updated (confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/stop-batcher-oscillation).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: shortflow-immortalize might reduce batching efficiency for long-context customers under extreme sustained long workloads. Mitigation: token bucket is per-tenant and configurable; default conservative allocation and ramp tests.
- Risk: monotonic clock change may surface other timing assumptions. Mitigation: unit tests and staging validation; gradual canary.

Success criteria:
- Hosted and Dedicated impacted customer clusters show restoration of short QPS to within 95% of pre-incident baseline within 30 minutes of enabling the flag.
- 99th latency for short flows reduced by at least 50% from incident peak during canary.
- No >5% regression in token-per-second efficiency or total tokenized batching throughput across canary hosts.

comments: 2026-03-01: Triage call with oncall and SREs. Incident matched pattern seen in earlier tickets but with a novel host-clock-drift component. Assigned to Ethan for root cause analysis. (Maya)

2026-03-03: RCA completed: confirmed eviction spikes coincide with admission clamps using timeline correlation. Reproduced locally by introducing 50-200ms monotonic tick skew. Decision: implement debounce + monotonic alignment. (Ethan)

2026-03-04: Design review with Runtime and Serving teams. Agreed to add per-tenant shortflow token bucket instead of global priority to avoid cross-tenant unfairness. Action: create PR and tests. (Design review notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Batcher+Oscillation+Meeting)
2026-03-06: PR opened (runtime/pull/1423). Initial unit tests added. Requesting review from @Luca Moreau and @Priya Shah. (Ethan)

2026-03-08: Load test in staging shows shortflow QPS restored and batch sizes slightly reduced (expected). No customer-visible regressions in long-context throughput in 2-hour soak. Added additional integration test for eviction edgecases. (SRE)
2026-03-09: Security review not required for this change. Prepared runbook draft and customer communication template. (Maya)
2026-03-10: QA started canary on 3% of hosts in Hosted. Monitoring dashboards wired. Next: validate 48-hour canary metrics then proceed to Dedicated staging. (Ethan)
